newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit up sharply on fund selling,tightening talk.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit up sharply on fund selling,tightening talk.

text.p: The ringgit broke below 2.50 a dollar in early London trading on selling by U.S. funds and talk that Malaysia may tighten monetary policy further, dealers in Singapore and London said on Tuesday.
They said funds sold between $30-40 million in the thin London market for Asian exotic currencies to push the ringgit to a high of 2.4970/80 a dollar around 1030 GMT.
"U.S. funds started the ball rolling just after lunch time in the Far East. They are looking to get back into ringgit," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in London.
He said many funds which had been selling ringgit against the Singapore dollar and the U.S. dollar were getting back into the Malaysian currency for higher yield and strong fundamentals.
"After failing to break 2.5140 last week, they are buying dollar/Sing and dumping dollar/Malay," a dealer with a Singapore based European bank said.
London-based dealers said ringgit's rise could be capped at 2.4950/60. It hit a low of 2.5065/75 in early Asian trading.
Research firm I.D.E.A. said the ringgit had scope to gain on talk of further tightening in the domestic money market. The interbank rates have risen substantially in the last two weeks.
"Although we believe a tightening is unlikely, the ringgit nevertheless has scope for further gains," it said in a comment.
I.D.E.A. said the rumours of tightening were triggered by the tightness in the money market, which have pushed interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange into a premium over spot rates.
The overnight rate in Malaysia has hit a high of 8.7 percent over the last few sessions. One-week money has risen nearly 100 basis points to 8.10/20 percent.
On Tuesday, one-month money rose to 7.50/55 percent, nearly 30 basis points higher than a week ago.
In the last two weeks, the ringgit has declined to a low of 2.5140 a dollar from 2.4760 more than two weeks ago.
